clue.text: Sport's governing body invested in game — it ought to be playable

indicators.note: to be invested in something is to be put inside it, like money in a firm, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
the ICC, the International Cricket Council, governs world cricket

explanation.surface: A sporting authority pours money into a game, insisting it be made fit to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it ought to be playable' reads like a complaint about the game, but it is the definition: an instrument is something you play.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical instrument, here the small high flute, is a thing made to be played.

clue.text: Cook's bipolar disorder

indicators.note: disorder suggests the letters of the word before it are jumbled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A chef is said to suffer from a mood condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorder' looks medical, completing the phrase 'bipolar disorder', but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To parboil is to boil food partly, one way of preparing it with heat.

clue.text: Performed slapstick for example — boxing glove not unknown

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, as a box holds its contents, so one piece wraps around the other
not means take away, and unknown is an algebra unknown letter, here the letter y

parts.note: slapstick is a kind of comedy
y is one of the unknowns in algebra
a mitt is a glove

explanation.surface: A clown performed knockabout comedy wearing a boxing glove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing glove' reads as one item, but 'boxing' is the containment signal, and 'unknown' is the algebra letter Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To commit a crime or an act is to perform or carry it out.

clue.text: Free newspaper replacing page frequently

indicators.note: one piece takes the place of another, with the newspaper standing in for the page

parts.note: open, as in an open position, means free or unrestricted
FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A free newspaper is used in place of a page, again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Often is an adverb synonym for frequently, both meaning many times.

clue.text: Oprah's broadcast reaching new generation — it's an institution

indicators.note: reaching means arriving at the next pieces, so they follow on
broadcast also means scattered widely, so the letters of the name are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: Oprah Winfrey, the American talk-show host
an age is a generation or era

explanation.surface: Oprah's show reaches a young audience and becomes a national institution.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Oprah's is read as 'is'. 'broadcast' fits the TV surface but shuffles OPRAH into ORPHA.
explanation.definitionFit: An orphanage is a residential establishment caring for parentless children, a classic example of an institution.

clue.text: Joking around, with sons instead of daughters, is just touching

indicators.note: instead of means one thing takes the place of another, so the sons replace the daughters

parts.note: kidding means joking around
D is the abbreviation for daughter, so two of them give DD
S is the abbreviation for son, so two of them give SS

explanation.surface: Horseplay with the boys instead of the girls stays harmless, merely a matter of touching.
explanation.walkthrough: KIDDING has two Ds, so plural daughters gives DD and plural sons SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Objects that are kissing are just in contact, as balls in snooker that barely meet.

clue.text: Jack's vocal part of church

indicators.note: vocal means spoken, so the word is the one that sounds like what follows when said

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church

explanation.surface: A man named Jack sings his part in the church choir.
explanation.walkthrough: The K of the answer is silent, so it sounds just like NAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: In playing cards the jack is also called the knave, the court card below the queen.

clue.text: Suspect smack and, initially, grass

parts.note: to smack of something is to smell of it, so smack and smell are close in sense

indicators.note: initially points to the very first letter of the next word only

parts.note: a grass is British slang for an informer, as is a rat

explanation.surface: Sounds like an investigator's suspicion about heroin and an informer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smack' and 'grass' look like drug slang (heroin and cannabis), but they are SMELL and RAT, and 'grass' is British slang for someone who tells the police.
explanation.definitionFit: To smell a rat is the idiom for sensing that something is wrong, that is, to suspect it.

clue.text: 1 Across essentially cleared out notorious clubs

parts.note: 1 is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: essentially means at its core, so take the central letters of the word
a word cleared out has its insides removed, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: Looks like a cross-reference: the flute from 1 Across drives off a band of notorious nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 Across' seems to point to PICCOLO, but it is read literally: 1 gives I, and the heart of ACROSS gives RO.
explanation.definitionFit: Irons are golf clubs with metal heads, numbered by loft.

clue.text: Pick up planting at herbaceous border pruned seven times

indicators.note: the outer words of the stretch are cut back by seven letters each, the front of planting and the tail of herbaceous, leaving letters hidden inside

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: collect the clippings after cutting back the flowerbed seven times.
explanation.walkthrough: Cut seven letters off the front of 'planting' and seven off the back of 'herbaceous', and what remains, with 'at' between, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather things is to collect them, so it is a synonym of pick up.

clue.text: Send clock back

indicators.note: back means the word is read in the backwards direction

parts.note: a timer is a clock that measures time

explanation.surface: An instruction to return a clock to the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clock back' suggests putting the clocks back an hour; instead TIMER is turned around.
explanation.definitionFit: To remit is to send money or a payment, a synonym of send.

clue.text: Exhausted and surprisingly due to perform first

indicators.note: first places this piece at the front, ahead of the rest

parts.note: to play a part is to perform it

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters come out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Worn out, and unexpectedly scheduled to go on stage first.
explanation.definitionFit: Played out means used up or worn out, so it shares the sense of exhausted.

clue.text: Conan has book out — relish wanting central character to find the right direction

indicators.note: out means removed, so the abbreviation for book is taken out of the name

parts.note: Conan O'Brien, the American talk-show host

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the middle letter of the word goes

parts.note: to relish something is to taste it with pleasure; a taste is also a liking

explanation.surface: A talk-show host brings out a book, and a relish loses its main character, before finding the right way.
explanation.walkthrough: Conan is the TV host Conan O'Brien: OBRIEN without B gives ORIEN; TASTE without its middle S gives TATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To orientate oneself is to work out one's position and bearing, as with a compass.

clue.text: Some wheel, silently spinning yarn

indicators.note: spinning means turning around, so the hidden letters are read backwards
some means only part of the words that follow is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A spinning wheel turns quietly as it makes yarn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning yarn' reads as making thread, but 'spinning' turns ELSIL, found inside 'wheel silently', round.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine, strong cotton thread, used for stockings, so a kind of yarn.

clue.text: Using last bit of petrol for power in Biden's car?

indicators.note: for means instead of, so one letter replaces another

parts.note: Joe Biden was POTUS, the President of the United States
P is the physics abbreviation for power

indicators.note: the last bit of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Biden's car running on its last drop of petrol.
explanation.walkthrough: POTUS is the acronym for the US President; swapping its P for L, the end of 'petrol', gives a British sports car make.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotus is a British maker of sports cars, so the answer is an example of a car, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Firm dates up quickly

indicators.note: up as in things being stirred up or disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: fast means quickly

explanation.surface: A company moves its dates forward in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' suggests reading DATES backwards, but that gives SETAD; it is a rearrangement to STEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadfast means firm and unwavering, as in loyalty that will not shift.

clue.text: Sugar coating skin for old councillor

indicators.note: coating means covering all round, so the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: Alan Sugar is a British businessman, host of The Apprentice in the UK
derm is a word for skin, as in dermis and dermatology

explanation.surface: A sugar glaze as a skin, said to be for an elderly councillor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sugar' is the businessman Lord Alan Sugar, not a sweetener.
explanation.definitionFit: An alderman was a senior member of an English borough council, a rank largely abolished in 1974.

clue.text: Soap actor loses lead after advert heard regularly

indicators.note: after places the second piece behind the first
regularly means at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken
loses lead means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: an agent is one who acts, an actor in the general sense

explanation.surface: A soap opera actor loses a starring role after an advert is heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soap actor' looks like a TV star; 'Soap' is the definition and 'actor' is AGENT, losing its A to give GENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergent is a cleaning agent, and soap is one, so the two serve as synonyms.

clue.text: Blue bonnet in Charlotte's infancy? Far from it

parts.note: blue, of films or jokes, means adult or risqué
Charlotte is a US city, and in American English a car bonnet is a hood

explanation.surface: A blue bonnet worn by Charlotte when she was a baby.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlotte seems to be a girl's name but is Charlotte, North Carolina, so the British bonnet becomes the US hood.
explanation.definitionFit: Adulthood is grown-up life, the stage of life opposite to infancy.

clue.text: Supporter's three and out

indicators.note: out as in put out of place or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fan describes an American football drive: three plays and out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three and out' is an American football phrase for a failed possession; here 'out' shuffles THREEAND.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent is a follower or backer of a cause, so a supporter.

clue.text: President hard for Republican to beat

indicators.note: hard for Republican means hard in place of Republican, one letter replacing another

parts.note: Donald Trump, US President
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A president is hard for a Republican to defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard for Republican to beat' reads as a political verdict, but 'for' is the swap signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To thump someone is to hit them heavily, a synonym of beat.

clue.text: Every now and then skeptic visits outlet to get meat dish

indicators.note: visits means going inside a place, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a pore is a tiny opening, an outlet for sweat

indicators.note: every now and then means at intervals, so alternate letters are taken

explanation.surface: A doubter occasionally drops in at a shop for a meat pie.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the even letters K, P, I of 'skeptic' and put them inside PORE. A pork pie is a British cold pie of pork in pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A pork pie is a raised pastry case filled with pork, a traditional British meat dish.

clue.text: Butcher's closed — accepting fine over a little infection

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above, so this part comes first
accepting means taking in, so the first piece holds the second

parts.note: shut means closed
F is the pencil abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: a little of a word is just its first letter

explanation.surface: A butcher's shop is closed after a small outbreak of infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher's' is rhyming slang: butcher's hook = look. A shufti is also British slang for a quick look.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang for a quick glance: having a butcher's means having a shufti.

clue.text: Keep turning over Dr Who missing opening with Ace at the start

indicators.note: at the start places this piece in front of the next one
missing its opening means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: A is the card abbreviation for ace

indicators.note: turning over means flipping round, so the letters are read backwards

explanation.surface: A Doctor Who fan keeps re-watching the show, with the companion Ace up front.
explanation.walkthrough: Ace was a Doctor Who companion, which fits the surface; here she is just the A of a playing card.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoard is to keep and store away a supply, often secretly.

clue.text: Pirate almost at sea, no longer anchored

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are jumbled
almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A pirate is nearly at sea, having just weighed anchor.
explanation.definitionFit: Atrip is a nautical term for an anchor just lifted clear of the seabed, so the ship is free.

clue.text: Shilton catches Maradona's first half cutback, revealing limitation

indicators.note: a goalkeeper catches the ball, holding it within his hands, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Peter Shilton was England's goalkeeper

indicators.note: a cutback is turned back, so the letters run in reverse
the first half of the name is its opening four letters

parts.note: Diego Maradona, the Argentine footballer

explanation.surface: England goalkeeper Shilton stops Maradona's first-half cross, an echo of the 1986 World Cup.
explanation.walkthrough: Shilton was the keeper beaten by Maradona's 'Hand of God' goal in 1986; a cutback is also a football pass played backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A parameter is a set limit or boundary within which something must operate.

clue.text: Every year fashionable society's first to provide great care

parts.note: PA stands for per annum, Latin for each year
in means fashionable, as in the in thing

indicators.note: first here points to the first letter of the word only

explanation.surface: Each year, the fashionable set's debutante lays on a lavish party with great attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To take pains is to take great trouble, so pains is a noun for great care.

clue.text: I must follow awards speeches, initially in mother tongue

indicators.note: must follow means this letter comes after the rest
in means put inside, so the first letters go within the word for mother

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: Someone must speak after award acceptance speeches, first in their native language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mother tongue' reads as one phrase, but 'mother' is MA and 'tongue' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Masai is the language of the Masai people of Kenya and Tanzania, and a tongue is a language.

clue.text: Truss getting in to class A drug — make official…

indicators.note: getting in to means entering, so one piece is placed inside the others

parts.note: a form is a school class
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
Liz Truss, briefly UK Prime Minister in 2022

explanation.surface: The former Prime Minister Truss becomes involved with a Class A drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'class A drug' reads as one legal term but splits into FORM, A and E; Truss is Liz Truss.
explanation.definitionFit: To formalize something is to give it legal or official status, so it means make official.

clue.text: … suddenly rush information into court — quite the opposite

indicators.note: into normally means one piece goes inside the other
quite the opposite reverses the order stated, so the second piece takes in the first

parts.note: SP is slang for information, from starting price in racing
to court someone is to woo them

explanation.surface: Continuing the Truss story: a sudden rush of information into court, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken at face value, information would go inside court; 'quite the opposite' flips which piece holds which. The ellipsis links this to 26 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: To swoop is to move down or in suddenly, as a bird of prey does, so to rush.

clue.text: Time's Up movement's momentum

indicators.note: movement of the letters means they are shifted about into a new order; the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: The Time's Up campaign against sexual harassment is gathering pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' looks like part of the campaign's name, but it rearranges TIMESUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is the driving force that keeps something going, which is close in sense to momentum.

clue.text: Go after toys, principally to play with

indicators.note: after places the second piece behind the first
principally means first and foremost, so the first letter is taken

parts.note: go is a euphemism for urinating, which is widdle in British childish slang

explanation.surface: A child goes to play with toys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' is a euphemism for using the toilet; widdle is childish British slang for that.
explanation.definitionFit: To twiddle something is to fiddle with it idly, turning it with the fingers.
